candidates.old:
LDA flip
    BPL to_scroll_screen_right
    JMP scroll_screen_left
.to_scroll_screen_right
    JMP scroll_screen_right         \ grind: a tail call; the RTS (to_scroll_screen_right + 3) stays
    RTS
candidates.new:
LDA flip
    BMI to_scroll_screen_left_76cf  \ grind: right, the common case, falls through to its tail call
.to_scroll_screen_right
    JMP scroll_screen_right         \ grind: a tail call; the RTS (to_scroll_screen_right + 3) stays
    RTS
.to_scroll_screen_left_76cf
    JMP scroll_screen_left
candidates.summary: The player's scroll: LDA flip / BMI to a JMP scroll_screen_left placed after the RTS, so the right scroll (the common case: BPL measured always taken) falls through into JMP scroll_screen_right instead of taking a branch over JMP scroll_screen_left. 1 cycle saved a right scroll, 1 lost a left scroll; same bytes.
candidates.equivalence: Same instructions on each path: flip negative -> JMP scroll_screen_left (was BPL not taken then JMP), positive -> JMP scroll_screen_right (was BPL taken then JMP); flags and registers at either JMP are as before (LDA flip sets N/Z, branches change nothing). The RTS stays at to_scroll_screen_right + 3, the target of the three no-scroll branches (BNE/BPL/BEQ to_scroll_screen_right + 3), which still return at once. The block is the same 11 bytes (LDA 2, BMI 2, JMP 3, RTS 1, JMP 3) so use_player_position_for_mover_Y and everything after keep their addresses. to_scroll_screen_right is referenced only in this routine; the new label is unique.
candidates.relies_on: flip's sign is the scroll direction (bit 7 set = left), as the old BPL used. Layout: in the shipping build the block is &215E-&2168 (page &21); the RTS moves from &2168 to &2165 and the three branches to it (from &2154, &2158, &215C) and the new BMI (from &2160 to &2166) stay in page &21, so no branch changes page; nothing after the block moves.
